title: From Single-Chat Entry to Multi-Module Collaboration: ChatGPT Mobile Redesign Accelerates the Implementation of Proactive AI Services

content_html:
On November 20, 2026, OpenAI began rolling out a new interface design for the ChatGPT mobile app and expanded the Dots feature, previously available only to subscribers of the $100-per-month ChatGPT Pro, to ChatGPT Business Standard users and some ChatGPT Plus users.

The redesign places Dots in a dedicated tab at the bottom of the home screen. It also lets users pin commonly used modules such as Codex, Projects, and Images to the bottom navigation, shortening access paths to frequently used features, and allows manual activation in Settings. The redesign is currently being tested with Pro users aged 18 and older in regions where Dots is available, as well as a small number of eligible Plus users. It is explicitly not available in the European Economic Area (including the EU), the UK, Switzerland, and South Korea.

While expanding availability, OpenAI is deepening ChatGPT Health cross-platform capabilities and proactive interactions. After making it available to all users in the U.S. in July and adding Apple Health support, the experience now supports connecting to Android Health Connect, offering in-depth analysis of sleep and activity; Dots can read health and medical records, adjust workout times when there are schedule conflicts, or remind users about preventive care. On desktop, it also supports building custom workout-tracking websites based on health data, and related updates are rolling out gradually.

Against a huge base of about 1.2 billion weekly active users, this change reflects ChatGPT's shift from a single chat window toward a multi-tool hub and proactive assistant. Its feature tiering and region-specific rollout will also further influence the interaction patterns and subscription-tier design of mainstream AI apps.
